title: UFO recognized pages v1
description: What an offline recognizer read from the pixels of a file that stores no text: a PNG or a JPEG, which is one page however large it is. Emitted by `ufo text --format structure` on those files. Every coordinate here is approximate and is never an edit coordinate: the file stores pixels, so there is nothing at a line or an offset for an editor to write. A scanned PDF page reports the same reading inside the pdf-pages contract, beside the page inventory the file itself supports.

pageCount.description: Pages this source has. A picture is one page.

pages.description: The pages a recognizer read, in page order.

partial.description: True when this read did not return everything it describes, because a page's text was cut at the character bound.

scope.description: What this read reports and what it does not, in the source's own words.

recognizedPage.description: One page of pixels as the engine read it: its lines in reading order, and the engine's mean confidence for the page.

index.description: One-based page number. A picture is page 1.

chars.description: Characters the engine read on this page, before any cut.

confidence.description: The engine's mean confidence for this page, 0 to 100. A low value is a warning, not a refusal. A page the engine read nothing on reports 0.

truncated.description: True when this page's reading was cut at the character bound.

lines.description: The lines the engine saw, in the order it saw them. A wrapped sentence arrives wrapped, because that is what the page looks like.

line.description: One-based line number within this page's reading. It is the same coordinate a `find` recognized hit reports, and it addresses a reading, never a place to write.

ocr.description: What the recognizer did: the engine, the pages it read, the density, its mean confidence and the sentence that says recognized text is approximate.

notice.const: OCR text is approximate: it is what a recognizer read from pixels, not a text layer the file carries.
